title: A Digital Twin Framework for Liquid-cooled Supercomputers as Demonstrated at Exascale
problem: Liquid-cooled exascale supercomputers exhibit complex transient thermal and power dynamics that are difficult to model and predict. Comprehensive digital twins integrating power simulation, thermo-fluidic cooling modeling, and energy conversion analysis for existing systems are lacking.
motivation: Digital twins enable energy-efficient supercomputing through virtual prototyping, what-if scenario analysis, and systematic optimization of expensive exascale systems.
method: ExaDigiT combines three modules: a power simulator modeling electricity consumption under different workloads, a heat-and-coolant-flow model predicting how temperature and cooling liquid change over time, and an augmented reality visualizer. Using six months of Frontier supercomputer data for validation, it forecasts energy consumption (including losses from power conversion like rectification and voltage regulation) for real or synthetic workloads.
key_novelty: ExaDigiT is a digital twin—a computer model of hardware behavior—combining power simulation, temperature and coolant-flow modeling, and energy loss prediction for liquid-cooled exascale supercomputers.
contributions: ExaDigiT open-source framework for digital twins of liquid-cooled exascale supercomputers
Integrated architecture combining power simulation, transient thermo-fluidic cooling model, and augmented reality visualization
Comprehensive validation on Frontier exascale system using six months of operational telemetry
Analysis and prediction of energy losses from rectification and voltage conversion in cooling infrastructure
Lessons learned for HPC practitioners developing similar digital twin systems

metrics.energy_or_tops_w: Energy loss prediction from rectification and voltage conversion
metrics.accuracy: Thermal and power model validation against measured telemetry

limitations: Computational overhead of the digital twin simulation and scalability to other supercomputer architectures not discussed.
primary_theme: Digital twin framework for sustainable exascale supercomputing
